capture_method: Directory listing of the sub-agent sidechain real claude 2.1.258 wrote during Phase 4 Spike S: <CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/projects/<slugged-workdir>/<session_id>/subagents/, holding one agent-<id>.jsonl plus one agent-<id>.meta.json per child. CAPTURED: the session id, the two child ids, the file names and the layout they sit in — the only things E1's glob actually derives its evidence path from. AUTHORED: every age_seconds, because git cannot carry mtimes, and every case but active-two-children, which are timelines applied on top of the captured layout to reach each leg of the rung. A case's verdict is therefore a claim about OUR code given the host's layout, not a claim about what the host did.

cases.name: active-two-children
cases.why: The file set the capture actually had: two children plus their sidecars, both still being written. The 90s/30s spacing is authored — only the ordering matters — and E1 measures the newest, so the slot is retained.

cases.name: quiet-past-release
cases.why: The same tree after the children stopped writing for longer than subagentQuietReleaseSecs. E1 measures and the slot may be released.

cases.name: newest-child-wins
cases.why: The rung reports the NEWEST mtime, not the oldest: one child long finished must not release the slot a sibling still holds.

cases.name: only-meta-json
cases.why: The host writes .meta.json sidecars beside the transcripts. The glob is agent-*.jsonl, so a directory holding only sidecars is 'cannot tell', not 'quiet'.

cases.name: empty-directory
cases.why: An existing but empty sidechain dir is 'cannot tell'. Treating zero matches as silence would make this rung trivially true whenever the path derivation is wrong.

cases.name: missing-directory
cases.why: filepath.Glob returns (nil, nil) for a directory that does not exist, which must read the same as empty: retain.
